A man was walking his dog along the beach. When he saw a boy throwing starfish into the ocean. Curious he asked the boy "What are you doing?" The boy replied. "The sun is coming up, the tide is going out and if I don't throw them back, they will die" The man scanned the beach and saw hundreds of starfish. "But there are so many, how can you possibly make a difference?" he asked. The boy looked at the man as he picked up another starfish. Then throwing it back into the ocean he said. "I made a difference to that one"

Our Foundation

Recovery is not a destination.
It is a decision you make every single day.

The Next Right Thing in Recovery isn't built on theory. It's built by people who've been through it — who understand recovery because they've lived it, not just studied it. That's why they saw what so many programs miss: people getting sober, then relapsing, because nobody ever taught them how to live.

In 2023, The Next Right Thing in Recovery, a licensed treatment center, was founded by Cate Ockey — who also founded an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit: The Right Thing in Recovery: A Peer Connection Clubhouse. Two organizations. Two missions. One founder who saw the whole journey.

Can you imagine it? A community space where anyone in recovery can walk in, any day, and be with other sober people — some seasoned in their sobriety, some brand new to it — in a shared space that is completely free. No fees. No referral required. Most people finish treatment on a Friday and get wished luck. Here, there is somewhere to go on Saturday.

The Clubhouse was built because being sober and living sober are two completely different things — and the space between them is exactly where most people fall. The Clubhouse lives in that space.

“Most programs teach you how to stop using. We teach you how to start living.”

— Cate Ockey, Founder

Why We Exist

Nobody Taught Them How to Live

The Next Right Thing in Recovery isn’t built on theory. It’s built by people who’ve been through it, people who understand recovery because they’ve lived it, not just studied it. That’s why they saw what so many programs miss: people getting sober, then relapsing, because nobody ever taught them how to live.

To many people who have never lived with addiction, it seems like a no-brainer. Just get sober and life will fall into place. Sadly, that is not how it works.

Many people who grow up around addiction never get the chance to learn the skills everyone else takes for granted. How to clean a home. How to do laundry, cook a meal, open a bank account. How to interview for a job and dress for it. Social etiquette, professional etiquette, taxes, credit, budgeting, grocery shopping. The list is long.

When you grow up in a house with addicted parents, those lessons get replaced with worries. Where will you sleep tonight? How will you stay warm this winter, now that the rent money went to drugs and you are on the street again? How will you feed yourself and your younger siblings? Finding clothing and a safe place to hide becomes the priority, not education and life skills. For so many people, this is a familiar story: a whole childhood spent in survival mode.

And here is the hard truth. If you do not know how to live and function in your community, you will go back to what you know, because what you know feels safe and normal. Many people in recovery also carry criminal records, one more barrier standing between them and a fresh start. So is the feeling of being an outsider when you cannot rent an apartment or hold long-term employment.

The Formula We Believe In
Recovery Knowledge
How to get & stay sober
+
Life Skills
Work, budget, home, community
+
Health & Nutrition
Body and mind cared for
+
Community
Peers, friendship, belonging
=
A Life That Works
Sobriety that lasts

But picture the other path. If you are taught the skills to live, not just survive. If you learn the recovery tools and the life skills before being sent back into the community. If your basic needs are met. If you have a safe place to sleep with rent you can actually afford. If you have a job with a livable wage, not just one you could get, but one you have been taught how to keep. If your credit is on the mend and your taxes are current. If you know how to shop for food and live within a budget. If you have community ties and healthy friendships.

Then we believe you can and will maintain sobriety.

That is what The Next Right Thing believes: the knowledge of how to be sober, plus the life skills to maintain it, plus physical health and nutrition, plus lasting connection to peers and community, adds up to a life that works. Every person who comes through our program receives an individualized month-by-month plan, tailored to their needs, meeting them wherever they are in recovery.

Why We Exist

The Gap Nobody Talks About

Being sober. Living sober.
Two different things.

The Next Right Thing in Recovery isn’t built on theory. It’s built by people who’ve been through it — people who understand recovery because they’ve lived it, not just studied it. That’s why they saw what so many programs miss: people getting sober, then relapsing, because nobody ever taught them how to live.

To many people who have never lived with addiction, it seems like a no-brainer. Just get sober and life will fall into place. Sadly, that is not how it works.

Many people who grow up around addiction never get the chance to learn the skills everyone else takes for granted. How to clean a home. How to do laundry, cook a meal, open a bank account. How to interview for a job and dress for it. Social etiquette, professional etiquette, taxes, credit, budgeting, grocery shopping. The list is long.

It Is Never Just One Thing

Addiction Rarely Travels Alone

It stacks. First the family that broke before you did. Then the substance that promised relief. Then the trauma nobody ever helped you unpack. Then the social skills you never got to learn, because survival came first. Then the criminal record that follows you into every application, every lease, every interview — and the doors that quietly close because of it.

The system treats each of these like a separate problem. A separate waiting list. A separate case number. But it was never separate problems. It was one person, carrying all of it at once.

That is why the full continuum exists. Treatment for the addiction. Skills for the living. Community for the loneliness. A plan for the record, the credit, the resume, the housing — all of it, in one place, from people who have carried it too.

No matter how broken you think your story is,
you are not too far gone. Not here.

There is no starting point too low and no version of you we will not meet. To everyone else you may be one of hundreds on the beach. To us, you are the one.

Why This Exists

The Gap We Refuse to Ignore

In 2023, Cate Ockey founded The Next Right Thing in Recovery, a licensed treatment center. She also founded The Right Thing in Recovery, an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit, home of the Peer Connection Clubhouse. Two organizations. Two missions. One founder who saw the whole journey — treatment is where recovery begins, and community is where it lasts.

Most people finish treatment on a Friday and get wished luck. Here, there is somewhere to go on Saturday. Because being sober and living sober are two completely different things — and the space between them is exactly where most people fall. The Clubhouse lives in that space.

"If you are taught the skills to live — not just to survive — and you have community ties, healthy connections, and know how to function in society, then you can and will maintain sobriety."

— Cate Ockey, Founder

Core Philosophy

What We Believe

01

Healthy Community Connection

The opposite of addiction is not sobriety — it's human connection. Our programming is designed to rebuild authentic human bonds that make long-term recovery possible.

02

Life Skills Are Recovery Skills

Sobriety without life skills is a house built on sand. We offer classes on functioning in a sober life — budgeting, cooking, cleaning, credit repair, job interviewing — the practical foundation that makes independence real.

03

Meet People Where They Are

There is no one-size-fits-all recovery. We start where you are and build from there, because everyone deserves individualized treatment.

04

Lived Experience Matters

Many of our staff carry their own recovery journeys. That lived understanding isn't a liability — it is the most powerful clinical tool we have.

05

Dignity in Every Interaction

You are more than a diagnosis. Every person who walks through our door will always be treated with empathy and unconditional respect — as a whole human being, not a case number.

06

Community Is the Cure

Our Peer Connection Clubhouse exists because we believe that healthy community — sober friends, shared activities, real accountability — is itself medicine.

Where Our People Work

Rent A Husband

A handyman crew serving the Salt Lake Valley — interior work, exterior maintenance, and rental turnovers. Two to four people show up together with a lead who knows the job, so a homeowner's list gets finished in one visit instead of three.

We did not start a handyman company that happens to hire people in recovery. We started a company so that people in recovery would have somewhere to work. A paycheck is not a footnote to recovery. It is how somebody makes rent, opens a bank account, and eventually signs a lease with their own name on it.

Run by Koby. Licensed, insured, and an LLC — backed by a recovery center.

Get a job priced → In recovery? Put your name down
The Policy Case

Utah does not have a sobriety problem. It has a sustainability problem.

Research consistently shows that relapse is not a failure of willpower — it is a lack of systems in place. Leaving treatment without a safety net such as roots, sober community, and life skills means returning to survival mode. Return to use is the predictable outcome. The Next Right Thing in Recovery was built to interrupt that cycle — connecting the gap between just being sober and living a long-term life of sobriety.

Our model is designed with evidence-based and client-centered treatment in mind, and is built for the very people the current system is failing. This allows us to pave the way from sobriety to long-term community reintegration and stabilization.

Our dual structure — a licensed for-profit treatment center paired with a 501(c)(3) nonprofit Peer Connection Clubhouse operated by The Right Thing in Recovery — serves clients across the full continuum. Recovery is about connecting the gap. We serve everyone — regardless of where you are. Recovery has no county lines.

Serving Everyone, Everywhere

Our Programs

A full continuum of care — from structured day treatment through long-term outpatient support — built around one belief: recovery is about building a life, not just achieving sobriety.

Clinical · Structured
01

Day Treatment / IOP

Multi-hour daily treatment while maintaining home, work, and family. Evidence-based modalities, strength-based therapy, and real life skills no one taught — side by side.

Continuing Care · Long Term
02

General Outpatient (GOP)

Long term clinical support, life skills reinforcement, and community connection during the critical window after IOP. We meet you where you are and stay as long as you need.

Court-Ordered · Assessments
03

Domestic Violence Classes

Court-ordered DV offender classes and assessments that go beyond compliance — raising genuine awareness and teaching coping strategies that protect families.

Family · Child Development
04

Parenting Classes

Effective communication, age-appropriate discipline, child development guidance, and breaking generational cycles — for parents who want to fully show up for their children. Reunification supervision available.

Court-Ordered · Online & In-Person
05

DUI Classes (Coming Soon)

Court-ordered Prime for Life program available online and in-person. Evidence-based curriculum addressing choices, risk, and consequences — designed for lasting change.

Navigation · Coordination
06

Case Management

Individualized treatment plans coordinating every area of life — social services, healthcare, housing, legal navigation, employment, credit repair, and tax preparation.

Housing · Transitional
07

Transitional Housing / Sober Living

Temporary to long-term housing for individuals every step of the way — from treatment to permanent housing. We serve everyone, regardless of where you are. Stable housing is one of the highest predictors of sustained recovery.

Employment · Career
08

Pro Recovery Employer Connections

Our pro recovery employer partners enjoy working closely with our clients, fostering seamless reintegration into society. Our community partners build relationships, offer training, and create positions for people in recovery — aligned with each individual's skills and goals.

Free · On-Site · Daily · Nonprofit
09

Peer Connection Clubhouse 501(c)(3)

A free, daily community space operated by The Right Thing in Recovery: A Peer Connection Clubhouse — an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit. Most programs discharge you on a Friday. We built a place for Monday. The Clubhouse itself is medicine.

What Others Skip

Life Skills No One Taught

Many individuals in recovery missed the essentials most people learned along the way. We offer classes on functioning in a sober life — budgeting, cooking, cleaning, credit repair, job interviewing, tax prep, and navigating everyday systems. These are the life skills no one taught, and they are available to all of our clients.

Clinical Excellence · Lived Experience

Our Team

This team wasn't built from a résumé stack. Every single person standing behind this organization was chosen deliberately — because of who they are, what they've survived, and the specific way they show up for someone in the hardest chapter of their life.

Some carry clinical credentials earned over decades. Some carry something no degree can give you — the lived knowledge of what it actually feels like to rebuild your life from nothing. Most carry both. That combination is not an accident. It is the whole point.

When you walk through our doors, you will be met by someone who either has the clinical tools to help you, the personal experience to understand you, or both. That was built in, one hire at a time.

Why It Matters

Lived experience isn't a liability in this building. It is the most credible clinical tool in existence — and this team carries it.

How They Were Chosen

Not one person on this team was hired to fill a slot. Each one was chosen because of something specific — a story, a skill, a way of seeing people that nobody else here has.

What You Can Expect

Empathy at every interaction. That's not a tagline. It's how this team was built to operate.

Every Donation Throws a Starfish Back

Most people in recovery don't relapse because they gave up. They relapse because someone handed them sobriety and nothing else. No plan. No skills. No community. Just a discharge date and a prayer.

The Right Thing In Recovery exists to close that gap. Every program we run — peer support, life skills, the Clubhouse, transitional housing, job placement — is built around one conviction: that recovery requires more than clinical treatment. It requires a community, a plan, and someone in your corner who has actually been there.

As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, every gift is fully tax-deductible and goes directly to the people sitting across from our team every day in West Jordan, Utah. No overhead bloat. No corporate intermediary. Just real work, real people, and real change.

Two Days of Suds & Service

The Right Thing in Recovery Car Wash

Friday and Saturday, July 17 & 18, the community came through — around 70 cars washed over two days at Fellowship Hall. Kids with sponges, graduates with hoses, families waving pink signs on the corner. Thank you to Fellowship Hall for opening their lot to us, and to every single person who pulled in, donated, volunteered, or honked on the way by.

Clean cars. Good vibes. A community showing up for recovery.

Out In The High Country

Flaming Gorge Camping Trip

Tents in the grass, a camp kitchen under the canopy, horses in the valley, and a fire that never went out. The Next Right Thing family headed up to Flaming Gorge country to trade screens for sky. Thank you to everyone who pitched a tent, worked the cooler line, split the wood, and kept the circle going late.

Recovery looks a lot like this: people showing up for each other.

Partner Spotlight

Getting There Without a Car

No car is one of the quietest reasons people lose a job, miss a meeting, or drift back out of recovery. It rarely shows up on a treatment plan, and it ends more of them than anyone admits.

Community Partner

Salt Lake City Bicycle Collective

A nonprofit bike shop that puts people on wheels.

Refurbished bikes

Through Bikes-For-Goodwill they put rebuilt bikes back into the community, focused on kids and lower-income households.

Open shop

Put in hours on the shop floor and you get the tools, a bench, and somebody who knows how to fix it standing next to you.

Membership & classes

Individual and family memberships include free bench time, discounts on parts, and access to their community classes.

If you need a way to get to work, to class, or to a meeting — tell your case manager or call us. We’ll make the introduction.

💼 Life Skills in 60 Seconds

The stuff nobody sits you down and teaches. Tap a card, steal the lesson, use it today. Want the real thing? Every one of these is taught hands-on inside our program.

💰
The 50/30/20 Budget
tap for the 60-second lesson

Split every paycheck three ways: 50% needs (rent, food, bills), 30% wants, 20% savings or debt. Even $10 into savings counts. The habit matters more than the amount.

💳
Build Credit From Zero
tap for the 60-second lesson

Get a secured credit card, buy one small thing a month, pay it off in full, keep the balance under 30% of the limit, and set up autopay. Six months of that and your score has a pulse.

🗣
The 3-Sentence Interview Answer
tap for the 60-second lesson

Situation, action, result. “We were short-staffed. I picked up shifts and trained the new hire. We kept every customer.” Every question, same recipe. Practice three stories before you walk in.

🧺
Laundry, Decoded
tap for the 60-second lesson

Cold water for almost everything, colors with colors, and if the tag shows a square with a circle, the dryer is fine. When in doubt: cold wash, low dry. You cannot ruin much on cold and low.

🛒
The Grocery Game Plan
tap for the 60-second lesson

Never shop hungry. Shop the walls first (produce, meat, dairy), write the list before you go, and check price-per-ounce on the shelf tag, not the sticker price. Frozen vegetables are not cheating.

🔑
First Apartment, First Try
tap for the 60-second lesson

Landlords check three things: income (aim for rent under a third of it), references, and honesty. Bring pay stubs and a reference letter to the tour. Ask about the deposit in writing — that is normal, not rude.

The 60-Second Reset

Craving, panic, or just a hard moment? Box breathing is the same tool first responders use. Four seconds in, four held, four out, four held. One minute changes your nervous system. Try it right now.

Ready
 
Credit repair, tax prep, job coaching, and every skill above — taught for real, one-on-one, inside our program.

Send a Message

A few quick questions
All optional — but every answer helps our intake coordinator get things moving before we even call you.
You did it. That was the hardest part.

Reaching out is the next right move — and you just made it. Someone from our team will personally call or text you within one business day, often sooner.

If you are in crisis right now — call or text 988. They are trained for this exact moment, available 24/7.

If you are not in crisis but want to talk to someone who understands recovery and can help you figure out next steps right now, call us directly at (801) 816-4977.

Thank you for showing up for them.

Reaching out on behalf of someone you love takes its own kind of courage. A member of our team will follow up with you within one business day to talk through options — what treatment could actually look like, how to start the conversation without it falling apart, and how we support both of you through this, not just them.

If things feel urgent right now, call us directly at (801) 816-4977 — you do not have to wait for a callback.

Thank you for the referral.

We take every professional referral seriously — Cate Ockey, our Founder & Executive Director, and our clinical team personally review every referral that comes through. Someone will follow up within one business day to coordinate next steps, including any documentation or intake details you can share now to speed things along.

If this is time-sensitive, call us directly at (801) 816-4977 so we can move quickly together.

Thank you for reaching out.

Community partnerships are how this organization actually works — from employer connections to corporate sponsorships, none of it happens without people like you. Cate Ockey, our Founder & Executive Director, personally reviews every partnership inquiry and will follow up within one to two business days to talk through what working together could look like.

Thank you — this means more than you know.

Every gift and every hour of volunteer time directly supports people rebuilding their lives. Ryan Anderson, our In-Kind Donations Manager, will personally follow up with you within one to two business days. Ryan is a drug court graduate himself and has poured everything into making sure every contribution actually reaches the people who need it — you are in good hands.

In the meantime, you can also donate directly here.

Thank you.

We received your message and someone from our team will follow up within one to two business days. Every message that comes through this form lands directly with our office — nothing gets lost, and nothing is too small or too unusual to ask about. We read every message personally.

Grateful Partners · September 2026

Sponsor of the Month

Recovery isn't built by one organization. Every month we stop and thank, by name, a local business that showed up for people rebuilding their lives — and tell you what their gift actually made possible.

Sponsor of the Month · September 2026

Minky Couture

A Utah company that makes plush minky blankets — and gives some of that comfort away.

What they gave

Five Travel Hugs blankets, each in its own gift bag, shipped to us free of charge. Minky Couture valued the gift at $930.

What it made possible

Their gift goes straight into our fundraising, and our fundraising is what keeps the Peer Connection Clubhouse open for people in early recovery.

Why it matters to us

They call this blanket Travel Hugs. That is close to what the Clubhouse is for: somewhere to land, and something steady to carry with you when you leave. A company built around comfort chose to share some of it with people who haven’t had much.

Visit Minky Couture → @heartofminkycouture

A gift to The Right Thing in Recovery, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit · EIN 93-4316358. Thank you, Heart of Minky team.

Beans & Brews

A Utah coffeehouse with shops across the state

What they gave: a gift basket for our fundraiser.

Nearly every recovery meeting you’ve ever walked into started with a pot of coffee. It’s how a room says stay a while. A local coffee company backing recovery just fits.

Help Us Find the Next Starfish

Point Us Toward Unmet Need

"The boy didn't wait for a program. He didn't wait for permission. He just picked one up and threw it back."

That's the spirit behind everything we do. Recovery doesn't wait for people to find it — it goes where the need already is. Transitional and sober housing. Shelters. Food lines. The neighborhoods where people are rebuilding with very little help, and haven't yet been offered a moment of genuine care.

If you see a gap — a pocket of your community where people are struggling and services aren't reaching them — tell us. Our team, our graduates and our community partners will look for the right way to help: supplies, a connection to services, or the right partner at the right moment.
